activities.description: Speaker introduces the topic of new technologies in journalism
Speaker discusses crowdsourcing as a new tool and gives an example of a reporter using Twitter to gather information
Speaker gives a second example of crowdsourcing where a newspaper uses a video posted online to expose police brutality
Speaker concludes by saying that each new form of technology has its place in journalism and gives an example of citizen photographers during a hurricane

scenes.contextualRelevance: The presentation highlights the importance and impact of new technologies on traditional and citizen journalism.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Technology is also providing significant new tools to make journalism better.
Crowdsourcing, the ability of the audience of you to inform the journalism is
exploding. At the Guardian in England they call this open journalism.
A reporter goes to Czechoslovakia to find out the former Czechoslovakia,
to find out what's being done to combat poverty. He puts a note on Twitter,
he posts on Twitter saying, I'm here, I'm going to be at this street corner,
if you have answers to this question, come and meet me, and is able to do a series
based on sources he never would have known that weren't in his Rolex.
A blogger says, I'm going to cover banking, I don't know anything about it,
educate me, and suddenly the audience becomes his teachers also at the Guardian.
The paper takes a photograph of a, has a photograph of a protester in England
who's been killed. The police say he had a heart attack.
The Guardian asks if anyone worldwide has video of the moment that he died,
a hedge fund investor in New York sees the post, checks his phone, has the video,
and establishes that he was killed by police.
Each of these new forms has its place. During a hurricane, citizen photographers
can be many more places than the journalists and anyone news organization
